question: The ‘Shiksha Karmi’ initiative and the ‘Lok Jumbish’ programme are schemes that helped increase the literacy rate of which state in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The 'Shiksha Karmi' initiative was launched in Rajasthan to improve the quality of education and enhance the literacy rate in the state.

• The 'Lok Jumbish' programme, initiated in 1992, aimed at promoting community-based education and making primary education accessible to all children in Rajasthan.

• Both these initiatives focused on innovative teaching methods, community involvement, and improving infrastructure in rural schools to boost literacy rates.

• These schemes have been instrumental in bridging the gender gap in education and increasing enrollment rates in schools in Rajasthan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Shiksha Karmi Project (SKP)**

• The Shiksha Karmi Project was launched in 1987 in Rajasthan by the Government of India in collaboration with Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (SIDA).

• Its main goal was to address teacher absenteeism and improve the quality of education in remote and rural areas by employing local educated youth as 'Shiksha Karmis' (education workers).

• The project focused on regular training, community involvement, and the use of innovative teaching methods to improve learning outcomes.

• The Shiksha Karmi Project received significant recognition for its impact on rural education and was considered a model for other states.

• **Lok Jumbish Programme**

• Lok Jumbish, meaning 'People’s Movement', was launched in 1992 in Rajasthan to create a decentralized and participatory approach to primary education.

• The programme emphasized the active participation of local communities, NGOs, and government bodies in planning and managing educational activities.

• It included various components such as school mapping, micro-planning, and the development of innovative teaching-learning materials.

• Lok Jumbish aimed to ensure universal primary education, particularly focusing on girls and marginalized sections of the society.
